### [Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741>)

Retrospection-Only Fine-Tuning trains an agent on its own explanations of attempted tasks while leaving the action trajectory as context rather than a prediction target. This suggests a route to learning from failed as well as successful experience without a reward-based policy update, with improvements demonstrated on coding tasks.

**Published:** 2026-09-28 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Self-Improvement, Coding, Experience Learning

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper gives the online training procedure, GRPO comparisons and behavioral ablations. Its no-verifier Qwen3.5-4B run reaches 49.2% SWE-bench Verified and 26.8% Pro after 20 updates versus 48.0% and 25.3% for GRPO after 40; submission history verifies September 28, 2026 at 17:54:24 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint primarily studying software engineering with Qwen3.5-4B; the mechanism is not causally established across domains. The method lacks independent semantic validation of self-generated explanations, and measured update/time efficiency is not a universal total-compute claim.
